Mina / team —

I reviewed Everline’s redlines and Mina’s draft. High level thoughts and a suggested path forward below. I’ve attached a focused redline (governing_law_and_injunctions_redline_20270211.docx) with proposed language.

Summary of our recommended approach:
1) Governing law: propose California law (contrary to Everline’s NY ask) for contract interpretation. California gives us clearer tech/IP precedents given our HQ and operations, which reduces legal risk.

2) Dispute resolution: keep monetary claims in arbitration (JAMS, San Francisco), capped to the disputed amount; preserve service and notice mechanics in the MSA.

3) Equitable relief carve (compromise): allow either party to seek provisional or injunctive relief in any court of competent jurisdiction to prevent irreparable harm, BUT include a short "break-glass" process:
   - Customer must provide 48 hours’ notice and an expedited escalation path to Redwood (email + engineering oncall) unless imminent harm is alleged;
   - Specify that seeking injunctive relief does not waive the requirement to submit any underlying monetary dispute to arbitration.

4) Forum selection nuance: we do not agree to exclusive personal jurisdiction in New York. If Everline insists on a specific seat, propose mutual choice of a neutral forum (e.g., Delaware or San Francisco) rather than one-sided selection.

Suggested next steps:
- If Everline will not budge on NY law, consider accepting NY law only if we get: (i) a mirror carve preserving Redwood’s right to seek injunctive relief in CA courts; (ii) a savings clause for enforcement of arbitration awards; (iii) a reciprocal waiver of jury trial.

I flagged specific language in the attached redline. Happy to walk through with the commercial team on a call.

—Laura
